title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Three silent regressions can no longer ship
summary: Nothing changes in the editor. Three behaviours you can see, and that no test was actually guarding, are now guarded: JUnit 5 results finding their test, the usage lens skipping private members, and test names with spaces.

highlights.title: Tests that check the code, not a copy of it
highlights.description: Several test files reimplemented the module they were meant to check. Each copy quietly drifted from the real code, so a regression in the real code broke nothing.

sections.heading: Under the hood
bullets: A JUnit 5 result named myTest() is matched back to its test, a nested class written Outer with a dollar sign is read as Outer.Inner, and an escaped quote in a failure message is shown as a quote. All three could be unplugged from the module without a single test noticing.
The usage count above a private member, and a Gradle test name written with spaces, are checked against the module now instead of against a copy of an older version of it.
A guard compares every expression a test copies from the source with its original, so the next copy that drifts fails the build.
